hinweis: Unified template data for the Briefing Generator on thorsten-litzki.de, merged from the earlier generator versions (V2, V3, V4, tl-campus Standard/Website/wp-optim, v5 B2B) and the coaching variant. Each field has label (short name), frage (the question to fill in) and beispiel (optional example). The origin of each template is listed under 'quellen'.

felder.label: Direct answer
felder.frage: What core question does the text answer, and what is the answer in one or two sentences? Put this answer at the start of the matching section.
felder.beispiel: Question: “How long should a brief be?” Answer: “As short as possible, as long as necessary: usually one or two pages.”

felder.label: Citable facts
felder.frage: Which of your own figures, data, studies or first-hand experience make the text worth citing for search engines and AI assistants? Include the source.
felder.beispiel: Your own analysis of 200 projects, metrics from Search Console, a study with a link

felder.label: Terms & entities
felder.frage: Which technical terms, brands, products and people should be named clearly and briefly explained?
felder.beispiel: Content brief, search intent, AI Overviews

felder.label: Question coverage
felder.frage: Which user questions (e.g. from “People also ask” on Google or from a content analysis) should the text answer explicitly?
felder.beispiel: What is a brief? · What goes into it? · Which mistakes should you avoid?

felder.label: E-E-A-T: Experience & expertise
felder.frage: How does the text show experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trustworthiness? Who is the author behind it?
felder.beispiel: Your own real-world examples, case studies, expert quotes, reliable sources, an author box with a profile link

felder.label: Deadline
felder.frage: When do you need the draft, and when the final version?
felder.beispiel: Draft MM/DD/YYYY, sign-off MM/DD/YYYY

felder.label: Contact person
felder.frage: Who answers questions, and through which channel?

felder.label: Resolving open questions
felder.frage: How are open questions collected and resolved?
felder.beispiel: A kick-off meeting, a shared document with comments

felder.label: Revisions & sign-off
felder.frage: How many revision rounds are planned, and who gives final sign-off?

felder.label: Stakeholders
felder.frage: Have all project stakeholders been informed? Who else needs to see the brief?

felder.label: Examples & references
felder.frage: Are there good examples of the style or content you want, internal documents or other resources?

felder.label: Re-briefing
felder.frage: Have all goals and requirements been understood correctly? Are there open points? Does the proposed approach work for everyone involved?
felder.beispiel: The contractor summarizes the brief in their own words and sends it back.

vorlagen.name: Content brief (blog post)
vorlagen.beschreibung: For blog posts, guides and landing pages with informational intent. The most used template.

felder.label: Primary goal
felder.frage: What should the article achieve for you?
felder.beispiel: Drive traffic to the website, build trust, win newsletter subscribers or leads, thought leadership

felder.label: KPIs
felder.frage: How will you measure success?
felder.beispiel: Rankings, time on page, comments, new leads

felder.label: Context
felder.frage: What is the context of this content?
felder.beispiel: Part of a campaign, part of a topic cluster, standalone article

felder.label: Reader persona
felder.frage: Who are you writing for? What problem or interest does this person have right now?
felder.beispiel: Marketing manager at a mid-sized company hiring an agency for the first time

felder.label: Audience language
felder.frage: Which terms does the audience use themselves? How much jargon can they handle?

felder.label: Pain points
felder.frage: What problems does the audience have with this topic?

felder.label: Key message
felder.frage: What is the one thing the reader should know, understand or feel after reading?

felder.label: Content angle
felder.frage: From which perspective is the topic covered?
felder.beispiel: Beginner's guide, expert opinion, case study

felder.label: Content type
felder.frage: What kind of content is being created?
felder.beispiel: Blog post, guide, white paper, landing page, social media post

felder.label: Formatting
felder.frage: Are there formatting requirements?
felder.beispiel: Plenty of subheadings, short paragraphs, lists, tables, infographics

felder.label: Word count / length
felder.frage: Roughly how long should the text be? A realistic figure helps with planning.
felder.beispiel: A comprehensive guide often runs 1,800 words or more, without filler. Use the length of the top results as a guide.

felder.label: Tone & style
felder.frage: How should the text sound?
felder.beispiel: Professional, casual, inspiring, technical

felder.label: Brand voice & style guide
felder.frage: Is there a style guide? Formal or informal address? Inclusive language, and if so, how?

felder.label: Primary keyword
felder.frage: Which search term should the article rank for?
felder.beispiel: “how to write a brief”

felder.label: Secondary keywords
felder.frage: Which three to five related terms belong with it?
felder.beispiel: “content brief template”, “content brief”, “writing a brief”

felder.label: Keyword placement
felder.frage: Where should the primary keyword appear? Usually in the title, H1, at least one H2 and the first paragraph, used naturally and without keyword stuffing.

felder.label: Search intent
felder.frage: What specific question does the searcher want answered?

felder.label: Meta title
felder.frage: Suggestion or requirement for the page title?
felder.beispiel: About 60 characters max, keyword at the front

felder.label: Meta description
felder.frage: Suggestion or requirement for the meta description?
felder.beispiel: About 160 characters max, includes the keyword, compelling to click

felder.label: Who already ranks?
felder.frage: Which pages hold the top positions for the primary keyword?

felder.label: Content gaps
felder.frage: What do competitors do well, what are they missing, and what can you do better?

felder.label: Unique angle
felder.frage: What makes your article better or different from other articles on the same topic?

felder.label: Outline (suggested)
felder.frage: How is the article structured?
felder.beispiel: H1: Keyword-optimized, engaging headline, e.g. “5 briefing mistakes that cost you dearly” · Introduction: a hook that addresses the audience's problem · H2: Mistake 1 … · H2: Mistake 2 … · H2: Mistake 3 … · H2: FAQ (frequently asked questions) · Conclusion: summary and a clear call to action

felder.label: Required elements
felder.frage: Are there elements or questions that must be included?

felder.label: Key elements
felder.frage: Which elements belong in the text?
felder.beispiel: Real-world examples, graphics, expert quotes, internal links

felder.label: FAQ section
felder.frage: Should an FAQ section answer common user questions directly? If so, which questions?

felder.label: Internal links
felder.frage: Which of your own pages should be linked? Important for SEO and user navigation.

felder.label: External links
felder.frage: Are there requirements for external links, for example to studies or trusted sources?

felder.label: Next step
felder.frage: What should the reader do after reading the article?
felder.beispiel: “Download the checklist”, “Book a free intro call”

felder.beispiel: 100 sales per month, 50 demo bookings, 5 inquiries for consulting projects

felder.label: Key KPIs
felder.frage: How will you measure success?
felder.beispiel: Conversion rate, average order value, number of intro calls booked

felder.label: Offer
felder.frage: What are the terms?

felder.beispiel: “Owner of a trades business, 52, who finally wants a predictable flow of new jobs through the website.”

felder.label: Problem (before)
felder.frage: What urgent problem, frustration or uncertainty does your customer have?

felder.label: Vision (after)

felder.label: Reason for the relaunch
felder.frage: What is the main reason?
felder.beispiel: Outdated design, technical issues, poor navigation, rebranding, new offering

felder.label: Measurable project goals
felder.frage: Which three to five KPIs define success?
felder.beispiel: +20% conversion rate, +30% organic leads, top 5 ranking for the primary keyword

felder.label: Project team & responsibilities
felder.frage: Who is the main contact? Who supplies content, and who owns design and development?

felder.label: Timeline & milestones
felder.frage: When is go-live planned? What are the milestones?
felder.beispiel: Design sign-off, content complete, go-live

felder.label: Content inventory & audit
felder.frage: Which pages will be kept (Keep), reworked (Improve) or deleted (Kill)?

felder.label: Keyword mapping
felder.frage: Does every important new page have a primary keyword and a search intent?

felder.label: SEO metadata
felder.frage: How will title tags and meta descriptions be carried over and improved?

felder.label: Content creation & migration
felder.frage: Who revises and creates the content, and by when?

felder.label: URL structure
felder.frage: Will the URL structure change? If so, what does the new one look like?

felder.label: Redirect plan
felder.frage: Is there a complete 301 redirect map (old → new)? Who is responsible for it?

felder.label: Crawling & indexing
felder.frage: How will robots.txt and the XML sitemap be configured? Are there areas that should not be indexed?

felder.label: Core Web Vitals & performance
felder.frage: Which targets for load time and interactivity (LCP, INP, CLS) are you aiming for?

felder.label: Audiences & user journeys
felder.frage: Who are the main users, and which tasks should they be able to complete on the site?

felder.label: Mobile first
felder.frage: Is the design consistently built and tested for smartphones?

felder.label: Internal linking
felder.frage: How does the design ensure logical, strong internal linking?
felder.beispiel: Breadcrumbs, topic hubs

felder.label: AI crawlers
felder.frage: Which AI crawlers may read the site, and is robots.txt set up accordingly?
felder.beispiel: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended

felder.label: Structured data
felder.frage: Which schema.org markup will be added?
felder.beispiel: Organization, Person, Article, FAQPage, Product

felder.label: llms.txt
felder.frage: Should an llms.txt file summarize the most important pages for AI assistants?

felder.label: Analytics tools
felder.frage: Which tools need to be set up?
felder.beispiel: Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console, Matomo

felder.label: Tracking plan
felder.frage: Which events and conversions need to be tracked?

felder.label: Go-live checklist
felder.frage: What happens on launch day?
felder.beispiel: Check redirects, verify tracking, request indexing

felder.label: Before-and-after analysis
felder.frage: Which KPIs will be compared before and after the relaunch?

vorlagen.name: AI video script
vorlagen.titel: Brief: AI video script for “[Video topic]”
vorlagen.beschreibung: For videos created with AI video generators. Describes scene, camera and mood precisely enough to use directly as a prompt.

felder.label: Video goal
felder.frage: What is the main goal of the video?
felder.beispiel: Draw attention to a new offer, explain a concept

felder.label: Key message
felder.frage: What one message should stick?

felder.label: Desired emotion / mood
felder.frage: What feeling should the video evoke?
felder.beispiel: Trust, excitement, curiosity, calm

abschnitte.titel: The scene in detail (who, what, where, how?)

felder.label: Characters (who?)
felder.frage: Describe the person or people precisely.
felder.beispiel: “A female consultant in her mid-40s with a warm, trustworthy presence, in professional yet approachable business casual.”

felder.label: Action (what?)
felder.frage: What happens in the scene?
felder.beispiel: “She sits at a tidy wooden desk and speaks calmly into the camera, as if having a personal conversation.”

felder.label: Location / setting (where?)
felder.frage: Describe the setting.
felder.beispiel: “A bright office with a large plant in the background. Soft morning light falls through the window.”

felder.label: Visual style & lighting (how?)
felder.frage: Describe the look.
felder.beispiel: “Warm, natural colors, soft light, a calm and focused atmosphere.”

felder.label: Opening scene
felder.frage: How does the scene begin?
felder.beispiel: “Wide shot of the room, the camera slowly moves toward the person at the desk (dolly in).”

felder.label: Main shot
felder.frage: What is the most important camera shot?
felder.beispiel: “Medium shot, from the waist up.”

felder.label: Camera movements
felder.frage: Are there specific movements?
felder.beispiel: “At second 15, a slow zoom onto the face”, “Pan to a whiteboard with a sketch”

felder.label: Key image / final shot
felder.frage: Which image should stay with the viewer?
felder.beispiel: “Close-up of a friendly, confident smile.”

felder.label: Facial expressions & gestures
felder.frage: Which subtle details should the characters show?
felder.beispiel: “Calm gestures with open hands”, “An understanding nod”

felder.label: Atmospheric details
felder.frage: Which elements reinforce the mood?
felder.beispiel: “Steam rising from a coffee cup”, “Blurred bookshelves in the background”

felder.label: Audio & sound
felder.frage: What are the audio requirements?
felder.beispiel: “No music, just the clear voice.”
